subject: Fitting ML with ctmm.select for elephant collars

messages.author: cfaa93bc8692cf13
messages.subject: Fitting ML with ctmm.select for elephant collars
parts:
hi Chris,

I've been running exploratory analyses on movements of male elephants of dispersal age, and I'm not having much luck with movement models (they just run and run in the processor). 

Collars should fix every hour, with 25,000-39,000 fixes per individual (collars have been on for several years to track dispersal strategies). I've successfully plotted variograms and went to select best-fit movement models with the intention of fitting AKDE HR estimates. Previously I had got through 4 of my 8 males with 15-60 minutes processing time, but one male ran overnight without a result, and if I set verbose = TRUE none of the models now finish running. Fitting with pHREML never finishes either.

I'm wondering if a sampling interval anomaly I spotted might be the reason, and if not whether my sample sizes are problematic. The intention was to run all data together, and then break down by season, dispersal stage and male age.

Thanks for any help

Vicki

*******

library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ctmm)
EReles <- st_read("Elephants.gpkg")
ctmmformat <- subset(EReles, select = c(extra__subject__name, fixtime))
rm(EReles)

ctmmformat <- ctmmformat %>% mutate(lon = st_coordinates(.)[,1],
                                     lat = st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
        st_drop_geometry() %>%
        rename("ID" = "extra__subject__name", "timestamp" = "fixtime",
               "longitude" = "lon", "latitude" = "lat")

# >>> this generates ID as chr, timestamp as POSIXct, longitude and latitude as numbers.

#make ele-by-ele format

ESP <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Esposito"))
PAK <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Pakwach"))
IBA <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Ibadan"))
GRG <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Garango"))
PET <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Peet"))
JMS <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Jameson"))
JAE <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Jaeger"))
LKU <- filter(ctmmformat, ID== c("Lenku"))

ESP <- as.telemetry(ESP)
PAK <- as.telemetry(PAK)
IBA <- as.telemetry(IBA)
GRG <- as.telemetry(GRG)
PET <- as.telemetry(PET)
JMS <- as.telemetry(JMS)
JAE <- as.telemetry(JAE)
LKU <- as.telemetry(LKU)

> ESP <- as.telemetry(ESP)
Minimum sampling interval of 59 seconds in Esposito
> PAK <- as.telemetry(PAK)
Minimum sampling interval of 56 seconds in Pakwach
> IBA <- as.telemetry(IBA)
Minimum sampling interval of 51 seconds in Ibadan
> GRG <- as.telemetry(GRG)
Minimum sampling interval of 51 seconds in Garango
> PET <- as.telemetry(PET)
Minimum sampling interval of 48 seconds in Peet
> JMS <- as.telemetry(JMS)
Minimum sampling interval of 54 seconds in Jameson
> JAE <- as.telemetry(JAE)
Minimum sampling interval of 1.15 minutes in Jaeger
> LKU <- as.telemetry(LKU)
Minimum sampling interval of 6 seconds in Lenku
*******

But when I manipulate the data in Excel (which I find easier to use for data checking), I get this (which conforms to expectations);

Row Labels Average of FIXINTERVAL Min. of FIXINTERVAL Max. of FIXINTERVAL
Esposito 01:04:08 00:00:59 04:00:08
Garango 01:04:17 00:00:51 23:08:15
Ibadan 01:00:41 00:00:51 16:59:58
Jaeger 01:00:13 00:01:09 00:59:37
Jameson 01:00:35 00:00:54 06:00:28
Lenku 01:03:27 00:00:06 00:02:41
Pakwach 01:00:11 00:00:56 17:00:17
Peet 00:39:28 00:00:48 00:59:42

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Fitting ML with ctmm.select for elephant collars
parts:
Hi Vicki,

Yes, those warnings are there for a reason. How far does an elephant tend to travel in 6 seconds compared to the GPS error?
  1. If you leave the data as-is and run a default model without location error modeled, then the models will all fit very poorly and could take a very long time to fit due to a multi-modal likelihood function.
  2. If you thin the data down to 15-60 minutes where you don't need a location-error model, then that shouldn't be an issue.
  3. If you keep all of the data and supply a location-error model, then the model can then fit that data much better, but you will be fitting many more parameters with a higher-dimensional Kalman filter, so this will be about 10× slower than 2.
  • In either case, the algorithms are O(n) and so processing 40,000 locations will take about 10× longer to compute than 4,000 locations.
  • In either case, trace=3 in ctmm.select() will give you a progress bar.
  • You should be able to trivially parallelize computation over multiple individuals with foreach, but then you can't see individual progress.
Best,
Chris

best things
Vicki
